content.text: : cortisol, as well as other steroid hormones, binds to intracell receptors – the steroid-receptor complex enters the nucleus and acts as a transcription factor to turn on certain genes, causing synth of specific proteins which are responsible for its physiological actions
Increases BG, increases protein catabolism from musc/bone, antagonist of insulin
Inhibits #/activity of cells involved in inflam response
Inhibits his release from mast cells
Mineralocorticoid effects: salt/H2O retention, potassium loss
: ↑appetite/wt gain, fluid retention, emotional instability, insomnia, indigestion, bitter taste, ↑BP/BG

: osteoporosis, GI (ulceration, bleed), psychiatric (mood, psychosis), cataracts, glaucoma, CV (HTN, edema, hypokalemia), diabetes, hyperlipidemia, Cushingoid syndrome, growth failure, impaired wound heal, adrenal suppression, IS
MOA: anti-inflam via multi actions on several types of WBCs
Stim gastric acid & pepsin prod -> take w food
Admin: IV for critically ill, PO, rectal
Admin: IV for critically ill, PO, rectal
: receptor = the β subunit of bact DNA-dependent
; binding alters its conformation and inhibits RNA synth; bactericidal
•effects ← his release – skin (flushing, rash, pruritis), flu-like syndrome
•color change (urine, sweat, saliva, tears → yellow, orange, red, or brown) = common but harmless
•also fever, rash, GI upset, bleeding problems, kidney failure; discolors contact lenses
•potent P450 inducer → many DIs: ⇣effect of OCPs, quinidine, corticosteroids, warfarin, methadone, digoxin, PO hypoglycemics; protease inhibitors + NNRTIs
: block late-phase rxn to the allergen, reduce airway hyperresponsiveness, & they are potent/effective anti-inflam meds
•reduce sxs, increase lung funct, improve QOL, & reduce risk of exacerbations
: ↑doses for prolonged periods may cause adrenal suppression, increase risk of fractures, & stunted growth in children
: binds to the 50S ribosomal subunit, inhibiting protein synth
•broad spectrum of activity: good against gram (+), gram (-), atypical organisms, & organisms other than bacteria (ex, Babesia microti)
•PNA, C. diphtheriae, topical use in acne
•less gram (-) activity compared w/ others in the class
: pts on Niacin or statins (↑musc toxicity)
•may increase levels of Warfarin, Digoxin, Theophylline, Carbamazepine, & statins (esp. erythromycin)
: binds irreversibly to the 30S ribosomal subunit, inhibiting bact protein synth; bactericidal
•there = a synergistic effect when combined w/ a beta-lactam or vanco
: slightly ↑activity against Pseudomonas; topical use for Keratitis
•ototoxicity (vestibular & cochlear) – cautious use of Gentamicin w/ other ototoxic drugs, such as Cisplatin, Furosemide, Bumetanide, Ethacrynic acid, & ↑dose NSAIDs
•Neuromusc paralysis – ↑musc weakness in pts w/ Myasthenia gravis
•needs to be renally dosed in pts w/ renal impairment
•monitor serum drug levels – peak levels are typically evaluated 30min after completion of the infusion
•trough levels should be drawn STAT b4 next dose = administered
